Lessons.Title: Which One Doesn’t Belong?
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will analyze numbers, expressions, geometric figures, and computations, identify your shared features and unique features, and use your analyses to complete or create Which One Doesn’t Belong sets.
This lesson allows you to apply your knowledge of various mathematical ideas from this course in generative ways. You examine sets of numbers, expressions, figures, or calculations, identify both shared and unique features, and create new items to complete Which One Doesn’t Belong sets. In the warm-up, you are given a full set of items.

2021 source activity sequence: Warm-up: Which One Doesn’t Belong: Strings of Numbers (10 minutes); Activity 1: Add One That Doesn’t Belong (20 minutes); Activity 2: Add Two That Don’t Belong (15 minutes); Activity 3: Add Three That Don’t Belong [OPTIONAL] (30 minutes); Cool-down: Reflection (5 minutes)
Math focus: A Which One Doesn't Belong? choice needs an explicit mathematical distinguishing feature; more than one defensible answer may exist.

Worked Edulytics example: Inspect all original numbers, expressions and figures before selecting an item. Name a feature shared by several entries and a feature excluding the chosen one. Explain the chosen answer with precise numerical, structural or geometric evidence. For 4, 6, 8, 9, only 9 is odd; different sets may have multiple valid reasons.
First-party Edulytics Cool-down (publisher's original not inspected): In 4, 6, 8 and 9, identify one item that differs and justify.
Original models, source figures, student-authored problems and teacher-scored explanations require separate academic review.

Original 2021 Which One Doesn't Belong warm-up explicitly displays number strings 0,4,8,12,16 and 3,6,9,12,15. First string is consecutive multiples of 4 beginning at zero; second is multiples of 3 starting at 3. Number 12 is in BOTH lists. These are observations that can support DIFFERENT justifications; the activity never requires one single unique outlier.

Activity 1 Add One That Doesn't Belong: incomplete four-option sets each need a new item and a stated shared property plus separate exclusion reason for each option. Activity 2 Add Two That Don't Belong: explain a common property of existing A and B and add two new items with coherent alternative criteria. Activity 3 Add Three That Don't Belong is explicitly OPTIONAL. Source graphics and learners' explanations are teacher-scored, not replaced by fixed numeric answer choices.

The pre-existing U07:L02 geometry-cards-number-talk exact family is reused ONLY as a small supporting card/classification and mental-arithmetic exercise. It cannot automatically grade source WODB sets, multiple valid justifications, or learner-authored entries. Student source-aligned work should be a teacher-reviewed open-response activity.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original two number strings: two legitimate observations
WorkedExamples.Question: Compare 0,4,8,12,16 with 3,6,9,12,15. What is a property of each?
WorkedExamples.Method: Look for common differences and divisibility.
Steps: The first list adds 4 each time, contains zero and consists of multiples of 4.
The second adds 3 each time and consists of positive multiples of 3.
12 appears in both: it is divisible by 3 and by 4.
A criterion must be explained: shared or differing features do not imply one unique outlier.
WorkedExamples.Check: Actual 2021 original two warm-up strings, but no alleged unique author answer.
